theme: Ahaz; the fall of Samaria, the northern kingdom exiled
readingInstruction: Read 2 Kings 16:1-17:41. These chapters give the fall of the northern kingdom. Notice the contrast between Ahaz of Judah and the kings of Israel, and read the long explanation in chapter 17 of why Israel fell.
settingTheScene: The prophets you have read in this unit, Amos, Hosea, Jonah, and Micah, spoke before this event. Now the narrator tells what happened. In 722 BC, Assyria captured Samaria and took Israel into exile, ending the northern kingdom that Jeroboam had founded two centuries earlier. The southern kingdom of Judah, under Ahaz, was saved for a time, but it followed the same path.
observation: “But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even burned his son as an offering” (16:3).
“And King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria… and saw the altar that was at Damascus” (16:10).
“In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he carried the Israelites away to Assyria” (17:6).
“And this occurred because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt” (17:7).
“Yet the LORD warned Israel and Judah by every prophet and every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways” (17:13).
“But they would not listen, but were stubborn, as their fathers had been, who did not believe in the LORD their God” (17:14).
“They went after false idols and became false” (17:15).
“They feared the LORD but also served their own gods” (17:33).
interpretation:
Chapter 16 describes Ahaz of Judah, one of the worst kings. He burned his own son as an offering, sacrificed at the high places, and when threatened by Syria and Israel, sent the temple treasures to the king of Assyria for help rather than trusting the LORD. Isaiah had told him to trust God (Isaiah 7), but he would not. He then copied a pagan altar he saw in Damascus and had it installed in the temple, pushing the bronze altar aside. A king who should have led the people to God remodeled God’s house to fit the world.

Chapter 17 is the theological summary of the whole northern kingdom. The fall of Samaria is told in just a few verses. The rest is an explanation. Israel fell because they had sinned against the LORD who had brought them out of Egypt. The list is long: they feared other gods, followed the customs of the nations, built high places, set up pillars and Asherim, burned incense, served idols, and sacrificed their sons and daughters. “They despised his statutes and his covenant.”

One line stands out. “They went after false idols and became false.” We become like what we worship. Those who worship empty things become empty. And the writer insists that God had warned them: “by every prophet and every seer.” The judgment was not unjust or sudden. It followed centuries of patient calls to return. Hosea, Amos, and others had given fair warning.

The chapter ends with a tragic picture. The Assyrians resettled foreigners in the land, who feared the LORD in a superficial way while still serving their own gods. “They feared the LORD but also served their own gods.” It is a portrait of syncretism, trying to mix the true God with others. The verse repeats: “To this day they do according to their former manner.”

The warning for the reader is plain. Hearing the word is not enough. The covenant requires faithful obedience from the heart. Judah is next, and the same pattern will bring them to Babylon.
connection: Jesus said, “You cannot serve God and money” (Matthew 6:24). Paul writes that the things which happened to Israel “were written down for our instruction” (1 Corinthians 10:11). 1 John 5:21 ends: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Romans 11:20-22 warns the church not to be proud but to continue in God’s kindness. Samaria later became the place of the encounter of Jesus with a Samaritan woman (John 4) and the gospel’s early spread (Acts 8).
application:
Ask what you fear and serve alongside God. Be honest, and name it.

Remember that you become like what you worship. Ask what you are becoming like.

Thank God for the prophets who warned and for the greater prophet who came.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you listen to what he has already said.
Ask him to keep you from mixing worship with the idols of your age.
Name one idol and give it to him.
